summary: Sen. Ed Markey (Democrat) ran for re-election and won over John Deaton (Republican) and other candidates.

candidates.name: Ed Markey
candidates.bio: Ed Markey is the Democratic U.S. Senator from Massachusetts and previously served in the U.S. House. He won the Democratic primary against Rep. Seth Moulton in 2026.

positions.summary: Says his focus is lowering costs, protecting workers and expanding opportunity, and contrasts it with Trump's agenda.
Supports Medicare for All and has criticized the cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Introduced the ICE Out of Our Faces Act and a bill to end legal immunity for federal law enforcement employees.
Introduced a Green New Deal bill to rebuild America's school buildings.
Is a sponsor of the Green New Deal and says the Trump administration should reverse its cancellations of clean-energy policies, including offshore wind halts.

candidates.name: John Deaton
candidates.bio: John Deaton is a Republican attorney and Marine veteran from Massachusetts. He won the 2024 Republican Senate primary and lost that general election to Elizabeth Warren, and launched a 2026 Senate campaign.

positions.summary: Has called for a temporary suspension of the federal gas tax and for a Clean Hands Act that would ban stock and crypto trading by members of Congress.
Says he would break up vertically integrated insurers and pharmacy benefit managers and require upfront disclosure of drug prices.
Says the U.S. should expand legal immigration while keeping zero tolerance for illegal immigration, and rejects abolishing ICE.
Favors using more nuclear energy and natural gas, and says Markey's plan has too many costly mandates that raise energy prices.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). 2026-11-25: not marked certified. Shares are from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's election statistics site, with blanks left out. A local news report (https://franklinobserver.town.news/g/franklin-town-ma/n/398885/galvin-crunches-numbers-near-record-mid-term-turnout) says city and town officials certified results Nov 18, but no Secretary of the Commonwealth page was opened that says the 2026 general election results are certified.
